title: Writing on one-nighters and sharing leadership
summary: They alternated home periods to write and had no ego conflict.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Then the other problem that came up was how to write when you're doing one-nighters. That really got me. So we
began to alternate, go home for three or four weeks at a time and come back with a bunch of stuff. That's how we kept it fluid, but not enough still. There was always the pressure there.
I don't know any other way to do it than that.
How did the two of you adjust to finding a band?

Neither one of us had that sort of ego problem; other ego problems, but not that one. As far as we were concerned, the music was what was important and I think the guys respected that too. It took the personality out of it, the music was there; not because of somebody's psychological--
(Side A of Tape 4 ended at this point. Transcript will continue with Side B.)
